name: Boma Nord
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Motingea Mangulu, Andre. 2004 (cited on Glottolog for Boma Nord); no online copy located

sources.citation: Maselli, Lorenzo, Véronique Delvaux, Jean-Pierre Donzo Bunza, Sara Pacchiarotti & Koen Bostoen. 2026. Nasal retroflexes in North Boma (Bantu B82, Mai-Ndombe, DRC). Phonological Data and Analysis 8: e1, 1-39. doi:10.1017/S2642182825000042
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 3 'North Boma phonology' (pp. 4-6) gives the consonant inventory (after Stappers 1986:1) and says the language 'shows stem-initial prominence' (a phonotactic/positional claim, citing Hyman 1998/2008), not word stress. Tone is treated as lexical (H marked, 'low tone is left unmarked', p. 32; fn. 19 p. 21: onset of a high-toned syllable is realised as a geminate). Nothing anywhere about stress, accent, or prominence of a particular syllable.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 2004. Divergences en dialectes tiene (bantou B.81): origine disparate ou perte séparée d'identité linguistique? Annales Aequatoria 25: 151-202.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The source Glottolog cites for Boma Nord, but it describes Tiene (B81) vs. Ikonya, not Boma Nord; Boma appears only as neighbours ('les Boma.. qui parlent des langues de zone B (Stappers 1986)') and in the claim that central Tiene 'se rattache au boma (Stappers 1986)'. Its section 2.3 'Tons' (pp. 165-167) is about Tiene/Ikonya (two level tones + rising/falling; 'en citation les mots sont généralement bas'); no accent/stress statement, and none about Boma.

sources.citation: Maselli, Lorenzo. 2024. Phonetic and phonological research in Mai-Ndombe: a few preliminary notes on rhotics and double-articulations. Languages 9(3): 114. doi:10.3390/languages9030114
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only rhotics and labial-velars; North Boma data from three speakers (Mushie, Bobala, Mbali). States (p. 2-3) that 'the literature on North Boma and Nunu is scant, with the main source of information on the former being the outline provided by Stappers (1986)'. No mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Pacchiarotti, Sara, Natalia Chousou-Polydouri & Koen Bostoen. 2019. Untangling the West-Coastal Bantu mess: identification, geography and phylogeny of the Bantu B50-80 languages. Africana Linguistica 25: 155-229. doi:10.2143/AL.25.0.3287234 (accepted manuscript)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Classification/identification paper, nothing on stress. Establishes identity: North Boma B82 = Guthrie's Boma B82 'inland from Mushie on the north bank of the R. Fimi and the R. Kwa'; 'The language spoken by this group has been documented by Stappers (1986)'; distinct from Boma Yumu B80z [boh], Boma Nkuu B80x, South Boma B80y and Eboo-Nzikou B74.

sources.citation: Stappers, Leo. 1986. Boma: eine Sprachskizze. Aus dem Nachlass übersetzt, überarbeitet und herausgegeben von Hans-Ingolf Weier. Hamburg: Helmut Buske. xi+76 pp. ISBN 3871187682, OCLC 17786227.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The one grammatical description of North Boma B82 (identity confirmed by Pacchiarotti et al. 2019 and Maselli et al. 2026); phonology chapter (consonants p. 1, minimal pairs p. 4, tone-marked data) is the only place a statement on accent/'Akzent' or tone-vs-stress for this language could exist. Held at MPI-EVA library (PL 8080 STA 1986); not online.

sources.citation: Maselli, Lorenzo. 2024. Documenting the sounds of the West-Coastal Bantu languages of the Lower Kasai region (DR Congo): an integrated phonetic and diachronic-phonological approach. PhD dissertation, Ghent University / Université de Mons, vii+391 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Modern instrumental phonetic/phonological documentation of North Boma (three speakers, 2021-2022 fieldwork); the most likely modern source for a prosody/tone/stress statement. Full text UGent-only, embargoed until 2029-06-21.
